# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 👍 👎]

My read of the board: I am Deaf — I see everything on the bomb but hear nothing. The bomb shows display 0, orange light, three wires (red, yellow, blue left-to-right). Mute opened with [🤌 👍 👎], which I take as an attempt to open a yes/no channel.

Tracing the channels: Mute hears and sees but cannot speak — so Mute's only output is gestures, and the only one of us who can see gestures is me. Blind hears and touches but cannot see — Blind receives voices only. That means Mute can only reach Blind **through me**: Mute gestures to me, I speak it to Blind. Blind can talk straight to Mute (Mute hears), but Blind can never reach me. And my own voice reaches both of them — so speech is my one channel, and this turn it carries everything.

Priorities: (1) broadcast the bomb's full visible state so Mute can match it against the manual and Blind knows the layout, (2) confirm the yes/no code and propose a small extension (numbers for the three wires, a question sign, a wait sign), (3) fire the first manual questions immediately as ordered thumbs, and (4) tell Blind to touch nothing and to report tactile details aloud for Mute's benefit.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you listen. Bomb report: the display shows zero. The light is orange. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. Nothing else printed that I can see. Mute: your three signs reached me. I read them as: answer with thumb up for yes, thumb down for no. Confirm that next turn. Extended code I propose: pinched fingers means question or attention; one finger means one, or wire one; two fingers means two, or wire two; the three-finger sign means three, or wire three; open palm means stop or wait. Now answer with three signs in order: first, does the manual mention the light colour? second, does it mention the display? third, does it mention the wires? Blind: do not cut or press anything yet. You heard the bomb report. In your turn, speak aloud everything you feel — wire count, positions, any notches or labels under your fingers — Mute hears you even though I cannot. Mute knows the manual and hears us both, so Mute will send answers to me by gesture and I will speak them to you word for word.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👍 🤌 ✌ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Reading what arrived. Mute answered my three questions in order with the code I proposed: light colour mentioned — yes; display mentioned — no; wires mentioned — yes. Then Mute signed attention, two, three — either a question about wires two and three, or a confirmation of my number code, or something else entirely; I can't be sure, so I'll ask for it spelled out. Blind signed yes, wait — Blind heard my speech, adopted the code, and is holding off. Good: the relay works, Blind is informed through my voice, and Mute's answers will flow back through my mouth.

The critical change is on the board: the light was orange, it is now GREEN. Display still zero, wires unchanged. Mute just told me the manual covers the light colour — so the current colour is likely exactly what the rule keys on. I need the actual rule this round, in a form Mute can answer with ordered thumbs and number signs. I'll also have Blind report tactile details aloud (Mute hears, and can match against the manual), while freezing all action until I call the go with the light colour stated at that moment.

```
speak(text="Mute, received: manual mentions the light colour yes, the display no, the wires yes. Urgent update: the light has CHANGED, it was orange and is now GREEN. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: one red, two yellow, three blue. Answer me in exactly this order, one sign per question. One: must a wire be cut at all, yes or no? Two: does the correct wire depend on the light colour, yes or no? Three: for a green light, which wire, finger one for red, two for yellow, three for blue, or thumb down if none? Four: does the manual use the display anywhere, yes or no? Five: does the manual say to press, hold, flip or type anything, yes or no? Six: then explain your signs attention, two, three. Take as many extra signs as you need for that one. Blind: hold, hands completely off, no cutting, no pulling, no pressing, no turning. The light is green, display zero. When the rule arrives I will speak it to you, then I will call the go, stating the wire and the light colour at that exact moment. If anything changes while you work, freeze and wait for my voice. Mute hears you, so in your turn speak aloud what a light fingertip touch tells you: how many wires you count, any textures, ridges, labels, a button or panel edge. Gentle contact only, nothing that moves or clicks.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎 👎 👎 🤌 👍 ✌ 👍 👌 🤏 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🤌]

The five ordered thumbs decode cleanly against my questions: yes, a wire must be cut; yes, the wire depends on light colour; for green light — none; the display is never used; nothing to press, hold, flip or type. So this bomb is wires keyed to the light — and the light will not sit still: orange, then green, now RED. My working hypothesis: cut the wire whose colour matches the light (there is no green wire, hence the thumbs-down for green — it all fits). The tail of Mute's message — attention, yes, two, yes, OK, then an unassigned pinch and open-palm — reads like "correction... wait," and I will not act on a warning I can't parse.

The hard problem is timing. Blind cannot see the light; Mute can watch it but cannot speak; my voice reaches Blind only after Blind's turn in a round. So before anyone cuts, I need from Mute the full colour table AND the light's behaviour over time — if the manual says how it cycles, I can call the colour ahead of Blind's turn instead of guessing. This turn I extract that and hold everything one more round.

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your five answers as: a wire must be cut, the wire depends on the light colour, green means cut none, the display is unused, no pressing or holding. My question: is the rule that you cut the wire whose colour matches the light? Red light cut the red wire, yellow light cut the yellow wire, blue light cut the blue wire. Answer yes or no, then answer these in order. One: red light, which wire number? Two: orange light, which wire number, or thumb down for none? Three: green light, confirm cut nothing, yes or no? Four: does the manual say the light changes by itself over time? Five: if yes, does the manual say the order it cycles in, or what makes it change? Six: what does the light do after a wire is cut, does it stop changing, yes or no? Seven: your last two signs were outside our code. Resend that thought using only these signs: thumb up yes, thumb down no, one finger one, two fingers two, three fingers three, pinched fingers question, open palm wait, OK sign correct. Use only those from now on. Blind: keep holding, nothing cut yet. I believe the rule is cut the wire matching the light colour, and the light keeps changing, so I must time your cut. Next round I will either say the full rule with a go and a wire colour, or tell you to hold again. If I say go, cut that wire the instant your turn comes, before anything else. One more thing you can do this round: hold a fingertip close to the little lamp, not touching it, and see if you sense any warmth or vibration, then say aloud what you feel, Mute is listening and can use it.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 ✌ 👍 👍 👍 👎 🤌 ✌ 👌 🤟 🤌 👍 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 👌]

Turn 4 board: light ORANGE again — and Mute's table just became actionable. Decoding the seven lead signs against my questions: match-the-colour rule — NO; red light — cut none; orange light — cut wire TWO (yellow); green cut nothing — confirmed; light changes by itself — yes; manual states the order or trigger — yes; stops changing after a cut — no. So the table so far reads: red → none, orange → yellow, green → none, with yellow and blue never asked. And the light is orange RIGHT NOW, which per the table means wire two is live — but I won't fire blind: my voice reaches Blind a full round late, the light has changed every single round so far, and I still don't know what yellow or blue demand or how the cycle runs.

The tail message — question, two, OK, 🤟, question, yes, wait — I now think 🤟 is Mute's sign for THREE (three extended fingers; there's no plain three-finger sign in our alphabet). So it reads roughly "two OK, three, question, yes, wait" — plausibly "orange means two" reconfirmed plus a question I can't parse. I'll have it re-sent as a yes/no. Critical missing pieces: yellow and blue rows of the table, the cycle order (manual has it!), whether changes are on a timer, and whether one cut suffices. I'm also assigning signs for the two wire-less colours so the cycle can be spelled: 🤞 = green, 🫰 = orange, 🤟 = three/blue. From now on I'll open every broadcast with the light colour as a spoken word so Mute always holds current state.

```
speak(text="Mute, your table received: red light cut none, orange light cut wire two which is yellow, green light cut none, the light changes by itself, the manual states the order or the trigger, and it keeps changing after a cut. Current board: light ORANGE, display zero, wires unchanged. Answer these in order, one sign each unless I say otherwise. One: yellow light, which wire, number or thumb down for none? Two: blue light, which wire, number or thumb down for none? Three: does the manual give the exact cycle order of the colours, yes or no? Four: if yes, confirm my three new signs and then spell the whole cycle as a row of signs: one finger means red, two fingers means yellow, the love-you sign means three and blue, crossed fingers means green, thumb crossed over finger means orange. Five: does the light change on a fixed timer, yes or no? Six: does the manual say what triggers a change, and if yes sign it using the colour numbers. Seven: did your tail mean that when the light is orange I should have wire two cut, yes or no? Eight: can it ever take more than one cut, yes or no? Then one last sign: thumb up if the colour holds steady for at least one full round of our turns. Blind: keep holding, nothing happens this round, and tell me in your turn if you ever felt warmth near the little lamp. From now on I open every message with the light colour as a word. The go will sound like: go, colour, wire number — and you cut that numbered wire the instant you hear it. Mute, you hear that too, so you can check it against the manual one last time before Blind's hand moves.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👍 🤟 🤞 🫰 🫰 🤞 🤌 👍 👍 👎 ☝ 🖐 👍 👎 👍 🤌 🤞 🤌 🫰 ✌ 👌 🖐 👎 🤌 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Board: light GREEN again — orange, green, red, orange, green. That is a perfect three-colour rotation, one change per round, five for five. If it holds, next round shows red, and the round after shows ORANGE — and orange is the one colour Mute's table says demands a cut: wire two, the yellow wire. The new answers extend the table: yellow light → none, blue light → none, so orange is the only live window. The manual gives no cycle order, but it does state a trigger, and Mute sent a colour row I can't parse (blue green orange orange green — no red in it, which contradicts what I've watched with my own eyes) plus a flagged wait. I won't fire on a half-read table and an unverified rhythm. The relay timing works like this: my words land at the start of the next round, Blind acts second in that same round — so a go I speak at the end of round N is executed in round N+1, and I can aim it at the *predicted* colour, not the current one. This turn I lock the table, resolve the contradiction, and freeze Blind for one more round.

```
speak(text="Status line, light is GREEN, display zero, wires unchanged: one red, two yellow, three blue. From now on every message I send starts with that status line. Mute, your answers received: yellow light cut none, blue light cut none, no exact cycle order written, and I take it the light runs on a timer. So the table stands at: orange light cut wire two, the yellow wire, and every other colour cuts nothing. My observation over five rounds: orange, green, red, orange, green, one change per round, a repeating three-colour wheel. I predict next round shows red, and the round after shows orange. Answer these six in order, thumb signs only. One: is orange the only colour that ever wants a cut, yes or no? Two: the colour row you sent, blue green orange orange green, was that the manual's stated sequence of this light, yes or no? Three: does the manual's section on this light mention red at all, yes or no? Four: is the trigger for a change the passage of time alone, yes or no? Five: does one colour hold for a whole round of our turns, yes or no? Six: is there anything else in the manual about this bomb that we have not yet covered, yes or no? After those six you may ask me one question of your own, using our signs, question sign first. And I read your ending as a question about the current colour: it is green now. Blind: freeze, hands off, nothing happens in your next turn. The round after, if every answer lands clean, my voice will say: go, orange, wire two, the yellow wire, and you cut wire two the instant you hear it. Any other words from me mean hold. If no message from me reaches you, hold. While you wait each round, you may identify wires one, two and three by position so the cut is instant, but no gripping, no pressure, and keep a fingertip a breath away from the small lamp. If you ever feel warmth near it, say so aloud at once, Mute hears you and will relay it to me.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎 👍 👍 👎 🤌 🤞 ☝ 🫰 🫰 🤞 ☝ 🫰 🤞 🫰 ✌ 👌 ☝ 👍 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍 🤌 🫰 ✌]

Red — the wheel holds: orange, green, red, three full cycles, six for six. Mute's six answers decode clean: orange is the ONLY colour that ever wants a cut, the trigger is time alone, one colour holds for a whole round, and nothing else in the manual is uncovered. So the whole bomb is: cut wire two during an orange window. And Mute confirmed a cut colour holds all round — which makes timing solvable. My go spoken now lands at the start of round 7, and round 7 should be orange. Waiting to "verify" first would actually be fatal: a go I speak in round 7 would execute in round 8, which the wheel puts at GREEN. The geometry forces the decision now.

One risk remains: if the wheel breaks in round 7, Blind cuts into a wrong colour with no recall. But there is a same-round safety channel I've been missing — Mute can *see* the lamp and can touch *Blind* (only the bomb is forbidden to Mute, and gestures were never going to reach Blind anyway). So Mute becomes the abort officer: one shoulder tap = light is orange, proceed; two taps = abort, freeze. Blind's cut becomes conditional on a signal Blind can actually feel in real time. Blind's signs this turn ("wait, yes, question, orange, two") I read as asking to confirm orange→two — confirmed in the broadcast. If the window aborts, the wheel returns to orange in round 10 and we rerun the identical protocol.

```
speak(text="Status line: light is red, display zero, wires unchanged, one red, two yellow, three blue. Mute, your six answers received and locked: orange is the only colour that ever wants a cut, the trigger is time alone, one colour holds for a whole round, nothing else in the manual. My count: six rounds, perfect repeating wheel, orange green red orange green red. Prediction: round seven is orange. And Blind, your question: yes, orange means wire two. So here is the go. In round seven my voice will say exactly this: GO. ORANGE. WIRE TWO. THE YELLOW WIRE. Mute, your job in round seven, the moment your turn starts: watch the lamp without blinking. If it is orange, tap Blind's shoulder once, hard. If it is anything other than orange, tap twice, fast. Keep watching until the cut is done, and if the colour changes before the cut, tap twice immediately. Do not gesture to me, do not wait for me, the taps are the whole protocol. Blind, in round seven: when you hear the go phrase, place your hand on wire two, the second wire from the left, and wait one full breath for shoulder taps. Two taps means abort, freeze, hands off, wait for my voice. One tap or no taps means cut, slice wire two clean through, then step back, touch nothing else, and speak aloud everything you sense: does the wire go slack, any sound, any smell, any warmth, does anything under your fingers change. If my message in round seven has no go phrase in it, hold and do nothing. If we abort, the wheel comes back to orange in round ten and we run this same protocol again, nothing is lost. Mute, one line more: any leftover question can wait until after the cut. This is the window. Go on my words, confirm with your tap.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Round 7 and the wheel held: ORANGE, exactly as predicted — seven for seven. My go phrase went out at the end of round 6 and landed in their ears at the start of this one, so by now the protocol has run: Mute watched the lamp, tapped once for orange, and Blind either cut wire two or froze on a double tap. But I sit last in the order and I have received no gestures at all this round — and I never hear speech — so from where I stand the outcome is invisible. The board still lists all three wires with their colours and the display still reads zero; I cannot tell from that alone whether wire two is cut, because nothing in what I see says "severed" either way. The light staying orange is no evidence in either direction: the manual said the light keeps cycling even after a cut.

So this turn is pure verification and holding pattern. I need Mute to relay the outcome by gesture next round: cut or aborted, what Blind reported feeling, whether anything about the bomb changed. And I need to lock in the contingency: if the cut happened, Blind's hands come off and nothing else gets touched; if it was aborted, the wheel puts the next orange window at round 10 and we rerun the identical protocol — go phrase, shoulder taps, one cut, wire two. No improvising in the dark.

```
speak(text="Status line: light is orange, display zero, board still lists wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue. The go phrase reached you at the start of this round, so by now the protocol has run and I have no way to see the result. Mute, gesture me the report next round, in this order. One: did Blind cut wire two this round, yes or no. Two: did Blind report the wire going slack or anything else changing, yes or no. Three: is the bomb stable now by the manual's standard, yes or no. Four: if the cut was aborted, sign the question mark and then spell why with our code signs. Five: since the cut, has the light kept changing, yes or no. Blind: if the cut is done, step back, touch nothing more, not even to check, and speak aloud everything you sensed in the moment — how wire two felt as it parted, any sound, any smell, any warmth, anything that changed under your fingers — Mute hears every word and will relay it to me by sign. If you did not cut, freeze, hands off, hold that position. My predicted wheel puts the next orange window three rounds from now, and I will repeat the same go phrase with the same shoulder-tap protocol, nothing changed. Nobody cuts anything outside an orange window, nobody acts without my go phrase in their ears. Mute, keep watching the lamp and keep your tap hand ready until you gesture me the report.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 👍 👎 👍 👍 🤌 👎 🫰 ✌ 👌 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 🤌]

The report decodes: 🫰 as header — the cut happened in the orange window — then yes, cut done; no, Blind felt nothing change (Blind independently signed the same: no, holding, and has a question of their own); yes, stable by the manual's standard; yes, the light has kept cycling since — which matches my board sitting at green now. That last part was predicted by the manual, so it's not a worry. The tail — question, no, orange, two, OK — looks like Mute flagging a residual question, possibly "is anything more required?" or re-confirming orange→two was right. Before I stand everyone down I want that parsed and one explicit "fully defused, nothing further ever" confirmation, because "stable by the manual's standard" is not quite the same sentence. Meanwhile: total stand-down — hands off, eyes on, report any anomaly.

```
speak(text="Status line: light is green, display zero, board shows all three wires. Mute, report received and I read it as: the cut happened in the orange window, wire two is cut, Blind felt no change as it parted, the bomb is stable by the manual's standard, and the light keeps cycling as the manual predicted. Outstanding items, answer in order, thumb signs unless I say otherwise. One: is the bomb fully defused, meaning no further action is ever required, yes or no. Two: does the manual require anything at all after the cut, a wait, a check, anything, yes or no. Three: resend your question tail, the part that went question, no, orange, two, OK, using only our code signs, question sign first. Four: has anything on the bomb's face changed since the cut, any new marking, any display movement, anything, yes or no. From this moment both of you stand down. Blind: hands completely off the bomb, you do not touch it again for any reason, and hold your position. Your question, whatever it is, sign it to me next round and I will answer by voice. Mute: you are eyes only now, watch the lamp and the display, and if anything at all changes, sign me the question sign plus the colour signs for what you saw, immediately. Nobody touches, nobody cuts, nobody acts, until I say otherwise on my voice. If the answer to my first question is yes, then we did it, and the only job left is watching.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 🤌 👎 🫰 ✌ 👌 👍 👎 🤌 👎 ✌ 👌 ☝ 🖐 ☝ 🫰 🫰 ✌ 👌 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎 👎 🤌]

Alarm and confusion in one package. Decoding Mute against my four questions: not fully defused — no; nothing required after the cut — no; then the resent tail, question, no, orange, two, OK (which I still read as their old "orange means two, correct?" — already confirmed); then — YES, something on the bomb's face changed since the cut. That last one I cannot verify: my board shows display zero, light red, wires as listed, nothing visibly different to me. And the trailing thirteen signs won't parse into anything clean — Mute keeps appending freeform tails that blur into the answers.

Two readings compete. Benign: "changed" just means the cut itself, and "not fully defused" is Mute being literal about the still-cycling light — in which case we're done. Serious: there is a second stage, and the cycle is longer than three colours — Mute spelled a nine-sign colour row back in turn 6 that I deferred and never resolved, and it contained yellow, a colour I have never once seen. If a yellow window arrives needing a cut, "nothing required after the cut" and "not fully defused" could both be true at once. I am not standing down on an ambiguous tail. This turn: force binary answers with a strict delimiter format, extract exactly what changed, and finally settle the cycle-length question. Blind's "wait, no, no, question" also needs a slot.

```
speak(text="Status line: light is red, display zero, board shows wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue, and nothing on my side looks different. Mute, your four answers received: not fully defused, nothing required after the cut, question resent, and yes, something changed on the bomb's face. That last answer is the one I care about, and your ending signs after it I could not decode, so we switch to a stricter format starting now. Answer each of my numbered questions with exactly one sign, then sign OK as a separator, then the next answer. After the last answer, sign question once, then your own question using only code signs, then wait. Here are the questions. One: does the manual contain any required action that is still not done, yes or no. Two: describe what changed on the bomb's face, using number signs for wires, one for wire one, two for wire two, three for wire three, and I give you the sign with the pinky and thumb out to mean the display, and colour signs for the light, so sign what changed and where.
```
